units.function: CLI contract tests covering Issue CRUD and its comments, approvals, read/archive markers, recovery, documents/revisions, work products, interactions, tree control/holds, attachments, labels and feedback-vote subresources.
units.dependencyDirection: The Vitest suite instantiates Commander commands through registerIssueCommands, supplies a local API base and bearer token, stubs global fetch and filesystem fixtures, and asserts the client-facing HTTP method/path/body/header mapping.
units.keyDataModels: Company/Issue/comment/approval/work-product/interaction/hold/attachment/label opaque UUIDs; document keys and revisions; recovery outcomes; interaction answers/option ids; tree-hold payloads; feedback targets/votes; run-id attribution header.
units.lifecycle: Parse CLI options; dispatch Issue/subresource HTTP requests; upload a local file as multipart with inferred content type and Agent Run attribution; inspect recorded fetch calls and selected request bodies.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 5/5 tests on 2026-08-19 and CLI no-emit TypeScript passed. Coverage is broad API-parity smoke testing, including a regression for X-Paperclip-Run-Id and MIME inference. It mostly asserts methods and paths, with little request-body validation and no server responses, errors, authorization, concurrency, idempotency, audit persistence or destructive-action semantics.
units.designRationale: Expose nearly all Issue-centered server capabilities through a scriptable CLI and use one compact suite to detect missing or incorrectly routed client commands.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a stable automation/API surface around Work that can manage collaboration, approval, evidence/artifacts, recovery and hierarchy control without bypassing accountable-human, data and execution policy.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the capability-parity matrix and explicit Run-attribution regression style. Redesign resources around Company OS Work, responsibility contracts, approval-bound action digests, evidence and stable error codes; generate or contract-test clients from the independent API rather than copying Paperclip command names and endpoint topology.
units.responsibilityConflict: A Run id header proves operational attribution only. The tested mutations do not bind requester, accountable human, delegated authority, exact action/config/data digest, approver, evidence and result; approval link/unlink and destructive/recovery commands can therefore appear equivalent to responsibility governance when they are not.
evidence: 8b85fdfa3cc855cda7620b56eaa4f85be0e26cd3 fix(cli): send X-Paperclip-Run-Id so agents can mutate their issues via the CLI (#7642)
2026-08-19 focused Vitest: 1 file and 5 tests passed
securityFindings: The fixed bearer token and UUID fixtures prove client wiring only; tenant membership, resource authorization, role/capability checks and token audience are not exercised.
Most state-changing request bodies are not asserted, so omission or corruption of approval reasons, recovery data, revision identifiers and destructive confirmations could escape this suite.
Update/delete/restore/link/unlink/release operations have no tested expected revision, idempotency key, action digest or durable audit receipt.

Attachment tests prove MIME inference from a filename and Run-id forwarding but not size/content validation, malware scanning, path safety, data classification, export policy or server-side media verification.
Interaction acceptance allows selected client keys or option ids, but the suite does not test mutually exclusive/invalid fields, stale interaction versions or authorized responder identity.
The CLI `--yes` confirmation is tested only for Issue deletion; many consequential mutations have no human confirmation or risk/approval contract at this layer.
